program_scope.purpose: Evaluate whether the repository's trait and host-resource reconstruction machinery can support a new ecological question about realized occupancy inside larval-resource geography.

ecological_question: Within the geographic opportunity supplied by larval host plants, why do butterfly species occupy some resource-available regions but not others?

conceptual_decomposition.larval_resource_geography: Union of native, extant, non-doubtful WCVP-v13 WGSRPD level-3 units occupied by all resolved species-level larval host plants.
conceptual_decomposition.realized_butterfly_geography: To be reconstructed later from butterfly GBIF occurrences, independently of the phylogatR genetic sampling coordinates.
conceptual_decomposition.resource_filling: Butterfly occupancy within host-available WGSRPD3 units; this is not estimated in the present reconstruction-only stage.

stage_1_reconstruction.target_panel: the exact frozen S1 339-species butterfly list
stage_1_reconstruction.rule: Reapply the existing HOSTS-to-WCVP-to-WGSRPD3 footprint construction to S1 species rather than joining S1 directly to the intentionally disjoint S2 500-species panel.

stage_2_response_blind_pilot_selection.eligible: S1 species with positive LepTraits host-family breadth and at least one native host-resource WGSRPD3 unit
axes: population-standardized log1p native host-resource WGSRPD3 unit count
stage_2_response_blind_pilot_selection.algorithm: deterministic farthest-point sampling in the two-dimensional resource-specialization space; fixed hash breaks exact ties

stage_3_future_occurrence_pilot.scope: Only the frozen ten pilot species.
stage_3_future_occurrence_pilot.requirement: Use butterfly GBIF occurrences, not phylogatR genetic sampling coordinates.
transport_design: explicit per-species total deadline propagated to individual HTTP requests
no species-level restart from page zero after partial success
stage_3_future_occurrence_pilot.first_diagnostic: Map butterfly occurrences to WGSRPD3 level-3 units and inspect whether host-available units contain enough occupied/unoccupied variation for a meaningful resource-filling analysis.
